question:
Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.
Peer pressure
P. when it comes to choosing the right
Q. course and, therefore, career path
R. and lack of guidance are some of
S. the reasons for indecisiveness
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. RSPQ.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct sequence is: Peer pressure R. and lack of guidance are some of S. the reasons for indecisiveness P. when it comes to choosing the right Q. course and, therefore, career path.

• Sentence R logically follows the subject "Peer pressure" by adding a second cause ("and lack of guidance") and introducing the verb "are", so it must come first.

• Sentence S completes the verb phrase "are some of the reasons for indecisiveness", giving the main clause its meaning.

• Sentences P and Q then specify the situation in which this indecisiveness occurs — "when it comes to choosing the right course and, therefore, career path".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: SPQR is incorrect because it starts with "the reasons for indecisiveness", which cannot directly follow "Peer pressure" without a verb.

• Option 2: QSPR is incorrect because it begins with "course and, therefore, career path", which makes no sense as an opening clause.

• Option 4: PQRS is incorrect because it places "when it comes to choosing..." immediately after "Peer pressure", breaking the required subject–verb link.

NOTE

• In para/sentence-rearrangement questions, first identify the segment that carries the main verb linked to the fixed opening — that segment usually comes first.

• Look for linking words ("and", "therefore", "which") as they signal which sentences must stay adjacent.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word ‘STRANGE’ from the given sentence.
The intriguing journal took a back place once more to the more mundane events at the Ouray inn.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Mundane.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Strange" means unusual, unfamiliar or odd. (अजीब, असामान्य)
◦ Example: He had a strange feeling that something was wrong.

• Its antonym "Mundane" means ordinary, commonplace or dull; lacking excitement. (सामान्य, नीरस)
◦ Example: After the thrilling trip, going back to her mundane routine felt boring.

• In the given sentence, "the intriguing journal took a back place once more to the more mundane events" — here "mundane" (ordinary) is used in direct contrast with "intriguing" (fascinating/strange), confirming it as the antonym of "strange".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Events is just a noun from the sentence and has no antonymous relationship with "strange".

• Option 2: Intriguing means fascinating or curious (दिलचस्प) — this is actually closer to a synonym of "strange", not its opposite.

• Option 4: Place is a neutral noun taken from the sentence and is unrelated in meaning to "strange".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "Strange": odd, peculiar, bizarre, curious, unusual.

• Other antonyms of "Strange": normal, familiar, common, usual, ordinary.

question: Select the sentences that contains no spelling errors.
option_1: People suffering from edzema have allergies with red and itchy skin.
option_2: People suffering from ekzema have allergies with red and itchy skin.
option_3: People suffering from eczema have allergies with red and itchy skin.
option_4: People suffering from ekezema have allergies with red and itchy skin.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. People suffering from eczema have allergies with red and itchy skin.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Eczema" — a medical condition in which patches of skin become rough, inflamed, and itchy, sometimes with blisters.
◦ Example: The doctor prescribed a soothing cream for her eczema.

• Spelling key: EC + ZE + MA. The word begins with "ec-" (not "ed-", "ek-" or "eke-"), is followed by "ze", and ends in "-ma". It comes from the Greek ekzema, meaning "to boil out".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Edzema" is incorrect; the second letter after "e" is wrongly written as "d" instead of "c".

• Option 2: "Ekzema" is incorrect; the "c" has been wrongly replaced with a "k".

• Option 4: "Ekezema" is incorrect; an extra "e" has been inserted after "ek", and the "c" is missing altogether.

NOTE

• Other frequently misspelt medical/skin-related words in SSC exams: diarrhoea, pneumonia, rheumatism, psoriasis, dandruff.

• When a word is unfamiliar, break it into syllables (ec-ze-ma) and memorise each part rather than the whole word at once.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.
Three novels and two story books had been written by him before 2020.
option_1: He has been writing three novels and two story books before 2020.
option_2: He had been writing three novels and two story books before 2020.
option_3: He had written three novels and two story books before 2020.
option_4: He wrote three novels and two story books before 2020.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. He had written three novels and two story books before 2020.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence "Three novels and two story books had been written by him before 2020" is in the Passive Voice, Past Perfect Tense.

• Rule — Past Perfect Tense:
◦ Passive: Object + had been + V3 + by + Subject
◦ Active: Subject + had + V3 + Object

• Applying the rule: the agent "by him" becomes the subject "He"; the auxiliary "had been" becomes "had"; the past participle "written" is retained; and the passive subject "three novels and two story books" becomes the object.
◦ Active: He had written three novels and two story books before 2020.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "has been writing" is Present Perfect Continuous, not Past Perfect.

• Option 2 is incorrect because "had been writing" is Past Perfect Continuous, which wrongly suggests an ongoing action rather than a completed one.

• Option 4 is incorrect because "wrote" is Simple Past Tense, which does not correctly convert a Past Perfect passive sentence.

NOTE

• Time markers like "before 2020" (an action completed before another point of reference) strongly indicate the Past Perfect Tense.

• Always match the tense of the active sentence exactly to the tense of the given passive sentence — only the voice changes, not the tense.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Irrevocable
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Irreversible.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Irrevocable" means not able to be changed, reversed, or undone; final. (अपरिवर्तनीय, जिसे बदला न जा सके)
◦ Example: The judge's decision was irrevocable and could not be appealed.

• Its synonym "Irreversible" means impossible to reverse or alter; permanent. (अपरिवर्तनीय)
◦ Example: The damage to the ecosystem was irreversible.

• Both words share the sense of finality — something that, once done, cannot be undone, making them close synonyms.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Unmediated (प्रत्यक्ष, बिना मध्यस्थता के) means direct, without an intermediary — unrelated to finality.

• Option 2: Congruent (सर्वांगसम, अनुरूप) means in agreement or harmony with something — unrelated in meaning.

• Option 4: Irresponsive (अनुत्तरदायी, प्रतिक्रियाहीन) means not responding or reacting — a different sense altogether.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "Irrevocable": final, unalterable, fixed, permanent, binding.

• Antonym of "Irrevocable": revocable, changeable, alterable.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
The sergeant could not stand the weather because it was __________ cold.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. bitterly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "bitterly" is used as an intensifier before "cold" to mean extremely or severely cold.

• Rule — Collocations of intensity: Certain adverbs habitually pair with specific adjectives in English; "bitterly cold" is a fixed collocation used to describe harsh, biting cold weather.
◦ Example: It was bitterly cold on the mountain top, and everyone was shivering.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "carefully" means in a cautious, attentive manner — it does not collocate with "cold" and gives no logical sense here.

• Option 3: "smoothly" means without difficulty or interruption — irrelevant to describing temperature.

• Option 4: "cautiously" means in a careful, wary way — again unrelated to describing the intensity of cold.

NOTE

• Other common intensifier + adjective collocations tested in SSC: bitterly disappointed, deeply concerned, highly unlikely, utterly ridiculous, widely known, fully aware.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into segments. One of them may contain an error. Select the segment that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
No talking / on the dinner table / is an absolute rule.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. No Error.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "No talking on the dinner table is an absolute rule" is grammatically complete and correct.

• "No talking" functions correctly as a gerund phrase acting as the subject of the sentence.

• "on the dinner table" is a valid prepositional phrase of place, and "is an absolute rule" correctly uses the singular verb "is" to agree with the singular subject "No talking".

• Since the subject, verb agreement, and prepositional phrase are all used correctly, the sentence contains no grammatical error.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "No talking" is grammatically correct — a gerund used as the subject of the sentence.

• Option 3: "on the dinner table" is grammatically correct as a prepositional phrase; it is not a subject–verb agreement or tense error.

• Option 4: "is an absolute rule" is grammatically correct — the singular verb "is" correctly agrees with the singular gerund subject "No talking".

NOTE

• In error-spotting questions, always check each segment independently for subject–verb agreement, tense, preposition, and article errors before concluding "No Error".

• A gerund phrase (e.g., "No talking", "Smoking", "Swimming") always takes a singular verb when used as the subject of a sentence.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.
The sailor tells great tales of adventure that you should take with a grain of salt.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Not take too seriously.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Take (something) with a grain of salt" means to view something with skepticism, or to not accept it as entirely true or accurate. (किसी बात पर पूरा भरोसा न करना)
◦ Example: You should take his stories with a grain of salt; he tends to exaggerate.

• In the given sentence, since the sailor tells "great tales of adventure", the listener is advised not to believe them completely — i.e., not to take them too seriously.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Great admiration (अत्यधिक प्रशंसा) is unrelated to the sense of doubt conveyed by the idiom.

• Option 2: Great patriotism (देशभक्ति) has no connection with skepticism or exaggerated tales.

• Option 4: Be afraid to refrain from (करने से डरना) distorts the meaning entirely; the idiom is about belief, not fear.

NOTE

• The idiom originates from the old belief that salt could neutralise poison, so taking something "with a grain of salt" meant taking a small precaution against being deceived.

• Related idioms of doubt/skepticism: "Take with a pinch of salt" (same meaning), "Read between the lines", "Cast doubt on."

question:
Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.
Birds’ heart, lungs and
P. uptake and intensive exertion compared
Q. to humans, which enables them to function
R. efficiently at these very high altitudes
S. muscles are more efficient for oxygen
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. SPQR.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct sequence is: Birds’ heart, lungs and S. muscles are more efficient for oxygen P. uptake and intensive exertion compared Q. to humans, which enables them to function R. efficiently at these very high altitudes.

• Sentence S must come first because it directly completes the fixed opening "Birds’ heart, lungs and" with the noun "muscles", and its verb "are" governs the whole sentence.

• Sentence P logically follows, completing the phrase "more efficient for oxygen uptake and intensive exertion".

• Sentence Q then introduces the comparison "compared to humans, which enables them to function", and sentence R completes it with "efficiently at these very high altitudes".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: QRPS is incorrect because it opens with "to humans, which enables them to function", which cannot directly follow the fixed opening "Birds’ heart, lungs and".

• Option 2: PRQS is incorrect because "uptake and intensive exertion compared" cannot immediately follow "Birds’ heart, lungs and" — the noun "muscles" (S) must come first.

• Option 4: QSRP is incorrect for the same reason — it does not begin with the required noun "muscles" to complete the fixed opening.

NOTE

• When a sentence fragment ends with "and", the next part must almost always begin with a noun/subject, not a verb phrase or comparison clause.

• Look for the segment that grammatically completes the given opening phrase first — it usually anchors the whole sequence.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
Something that is capable of being accomplished
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Feasible.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Feasible" means something that is capable of being accomplished or done; possible and practical. (व्यवहार्य, संभव)
◦ Example: The manager felt the new plan was feasible within the given budget.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Untenable (असमर्थनीय) means not able to be defended or maintained, e.g. an untenable argument — unrelated to being achievable.

• Option 3: Irrevocable (अपरिवर्तनीय) means not able to be changed or undone — refers to finality, not achievability.

• Option 4: Eligible (योग्य, पात्र) means having the right qualifications to be chosen for something — refers to qualification, not to whether a task can be accomplished.

NOTE

• Other common one-word substitutes with "capable of/possible": Viable (capable of working successfully), Plausible (seeming reasonable or probable), Tenable (able to be defended).

• Do not confuse "Feasible" (practically possible) with "Eligible" (qualified/entitled) — a very common SSC distractor pair.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
They were preparing banners with different designs for the sports meet.
option_1: Banners were being prepared by them with different designs for the sports meet.
option_2: Banners have prepared by them with different designs for the sports meet.
option_3: Banners had been prepared by them with different designs for the sports meet.
option_4: Banners were prepared by them with different designs for the sports meet.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Banners were being prepared by them with different designs for the sports meet.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence "They were preparing banners..." is in the Active Voice, Past Continuous Tense.

• Rule — Past Continuous Tense:
◦ Active: Subject + was/were + V-ing + Object
◦ Passive: Object + was/were + being + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "banners" becomes the subject; since "they" is plural, the auxiliary is "were"; "being" is inserted; the verb "preparing" becomes the past participle "prepared"; and "they" becomes the agent "by them."
◦ Passive: Banners were being prepared by them with different designs for the sports meet.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 is incorrect because "have prepared" is Present Perfect, and it also lacks the auxiliary "been", making it grammatically wrong for passive voice.

• Option 3 is incorrect because "had been prepared" is the passive of the Past Perfect Tense, not Past Continuous.

• Option 4 is incorrect because "were prepared" (without "being") is the passive of the Simple Past Tense, which fails to convey the ongoing/continuous nature of the original sentence.

NOTE

• The word "being" is the key marker of a Continuous Tense passive sentence — its absence usually signals Simple Past passive instead.

• Always identify the tense of the active sentence first, since voice conversion must preserve the same tense.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.
The anxious duke was found strolling in the garden to and fro.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Forward and backward.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "To and fro" means moving repeatedly in one direction and then the opposite direction; forward and backward. (आगे-पीछे, इधर-उधर)
◦ Example: The old man walked to and fro on the porch, lost in thought.

• In the given sentence, the anxious duke strolling "to and fro" in the garden suggests he was pacing back and forth out of restlessness.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: From north to south (उत्तर से दक्षिण) wrongly restricts the movement to fixed compass directions, which the idiom does not specify.

• Option 2: From west to east (पश्चिम से पूर्व) is incorrect for the same reason — the idiom denotes repeated back-and-forth motion, not a single directional journey.

• Option 4: Upward and downward (ऊपर-नीचे) incorrectly describes vertical motion, whereas "to and fro" describes horizontal, repeated pacing.

NOTE

• Similar idioms of repeated movement: "Back and forth" (same meaning as "to and fro"), "Up and down" (vertical repeated motion), "Round and round" (circular repeated motion).

• "To and fro" is commonly used for someone who is anxious, restless, or in deep thought while pacing.

question:
The question below consists of a set of labeled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
P. Basically, “smart farming” is applying information and data technologies for optimizing complex farming systems.
Q. With these tools, farmers can monitor field conditions without going to the field.
R. The focus is on access to data and how farmers can use the collected information intelligently.
S. The technology used in smart farming range from IoT and robotics to drones and AI.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. PRSQ.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct sequence is: P. Basically, "smart farming" is applying information and data technologies for optimizing complex farming systems. R. The focus is on access to data and how farmers can use the collected information intelligently. S. The technology used in smart farming range from IoT and robotics to drones and AI. Q. With these tools, farmers can monitor field conditions without going to the field.

• Sentence P must open the paragraph as it introduces and defines the topic, "smart farming".

• Sentence R naturally follows by explaining what smart farming focuses on — access to and intelligent use of data.

• Sentence S then lists the specific technologies (IoT, robotics, drones, AI) used to achieve this.

• Sentence Q concludes by referring back to "these tools" (the technologies named in S) and explaining their practical benefit — monitoring fields remotely.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: RSQP is incorrect because it does not begin with the definitional sentence P, which is needed to introduce the topic first.

• Option 2: PQSR is incorrect because Q (which refers to "these tools") is placed before S, which is where the tools are actually named — creating a broken reference.

• Option 4: SPQR is incorrect because it opens with a list of technologies (S) before the topic itself ("smart farming") has even been defined by P.

NOTE

• When a sentence contains a reference word like "these tools", "this", or "they", it must always be placed AFTER the sentence that introduces the noun it refers to.

• The sentence that defines or introduces the topic (often containing the phrase in quotation marks, like "smart farming") usually opens the paragraph.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Encourage
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Dishearten.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Encourage" means to give someone support, confidence, or hope; to inspire with courage. (प्रोत्साहित करना)
◦ Example: Her teacher encouraged her to pursue painting professionally.

• Its antonym "Dishearten" means to cause someone to lose hope, confidence or enthusiasm; to discourage. (हतोत्साहित करना, निराश करना)
◦ Example: The team's repeated losses disheartened the young players.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Boost (बढ़ावा देना) means to increase or improve something, which is a synonym, not an antonym, of "encourage".

• Option 2: Inspire (प्रेरित करना) means to fill someone with the urge or ability to do something, again a synonym of "encourage".

• Option 3: Energise (ऊर्जा देना) means to give vitality and enthusiasm to someone, which is also close in meaning to "encourage", not opposite.

NOTE

• Other antonyms of "Encourage": discourage, deter, demoralise, dampen.

• Other synonyms of "Encourage": motivate, hearten, embolden, inspire.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
The scientific study of plants and their structure
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Botany.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Botany" means the scientific study of plants and their structure, properties, and biological processes. (वनस्पति विज्ञान)
◦ Example: She is pursuing a degree in Botany at the state university.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Plantation (बागान) refers to a large estate or farm where crops such as tea, coffee, or rubber are cultivated, not the study of plants.

• Option 2: Environment (पर्यावरण) refers to the surrounding natural world, a much broader concept than the study of plant structure specifically.

• Option 3: Biology (जीव विज्ञान) is the general scientific study of all living organisms, both plants and animals — too broad to be the precise substitute for the study of plants alone.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes: Zoology (study of animals), Ornithology (study of birds), Entomology (study of insects), Horticulture (the art/science of garden cultivation).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
The number of students / attending their classes / are constantly decreasing / in our university.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. are constantly decreasing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject of the sentence is "The number of students", not "students".

• Rule — Subject-Verb Agreement with "The number of": The phrase "The number of + plural noun" takes a singular verb, because "number" (singular) is the actual head of the subject.
◦ Correct: The number of students is constantly decreasing.

• The given segment wrongly uses the plural verb "are" instead of the singular "is", making it grammatically incorrect.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "The number of students" is grammatically correct — it is simply the subject phrase of the sentence.

• Option 2: "attending their classes" is a correct participial phrase modifying "students" and contains no error.

• Option 3: "in our university" is a correct prepositional phrase of place and contains no error.

NOTE

• Contrast this with "A number of + plural noun", which takes a plural verb (e.g., "A number of students are absent today").

• Other singular-subject phrases that take a singular verb despite an intervening plural noun: "Each of", "Every one of", "Either of", "Neither of."

question:
Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the following sentence.
The problematic and convoluted situation concerning Rakhtim’s job is likely to exhilarate in the forseeable future.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. forseeable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Foreseeable" — able to be foreseen or predicted; likely to happen in the near future.
◦ Example: There are no changes planned in the foreseeable future.

• Spelling key: FORE + SEE + ABLE. The word is built from "fore-" (before, ahead) + "see" + "-able". The prefix "fore-" requires both the "o" and the "r" before "see" — the printed word "forseeable" wrongly drops the "e" from "fore-".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "convoluted" is correctly spelt — meaning extremely complex and difficult to follow.

• Option 3: "problematic" is correctly spelt — meaning constituting or causing a problem.

• Option 4: "exhilarate" is correctly spelt — meaning to make someone feel very happy, animated, or elated.

NOTE

• Do not confuse "foreseeable" with words that drop the "e" from the prefix "fore-"; words such as foretell, forewarn, forefather all retain the full "fore-" spelling.

• Other commonly misspelt "-able" words in SSC exams: noticeable, manageable, comfortable, reasonable.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Appropriate
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Improper.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Appropriate" means suitable or proper in the circumstances; fitting. (उचित, उपयुक्त)
◦ Example: She wore appropriate clothing for the formal event.

• Its antonym "Improper" means not in accordance with accepted standards of behaviour or method; unsuitable. (अनुचित, अनुपयुक्त)
◦ Example: Shouting during the meeting was considered improper.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Transparent (पारदर्शी) means easy to see through or understand clearly — unrelated to suitability.

• Option 3: Salient (प्रमुख, उल्लेखनीय) means most noticeable or important — a different sense altogether.

• Option 4: Disturbing (परेशान करने वाला) means causing anxiety or distress — also unrelated to the idea of suitability.

NOTE

• Other antonyms of "Appropriate": unsuitable, unfit, inapt, incongruous.

• Other synonyms of "Appropriate": suitable, fitting, apt, proper.

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate word. Choose the correct alternative.
Kajol is one age-defying beauty and her sari collection is worth __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. bookmarking.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "worth + gerund (V-ing)" is used to say that something deserves the action mentioned because it is valuable, interesting or useful enough.

• "Bookmarking" means saving or noting something as worth remembering or returning to; here it means Kajol's sari collection is impressive enough to be noted/remembered.
◦ Example: This website is worth bookmarking for future reference.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "repudiating" means rejecting or refusing to accept something as true or valid — it does not fit the positive, admiring tone of the sentence.

• Option 3: "flirting" means behaving playfully/romantically towards someone — it cannot logically apply to a "sari collection".

• Option 4: "renouncing" means formally giving up or rejecting something — the opposite sense of praising a valuable collection.

NOTE

• The construction "worth + V-ing" always uses the gerund form, never the infinitive (e.g., "worth watching", NOT "worth to watch").

• Similar positive collocations: worth mentioning, worth noting, worth considering, worth remembering.

question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.
Ramita said, “I wish I didn’t have to meet my step-mother.”
option_1: Ramita said she wished she hadn’t have to meet her step-mother.
option_2: Ramita said she wished she didn’t meet her step-mother.
option_3: Ramita said she wished she didn’t have to meet her step-mother.
option_4: Ramita said she wished hadn’t met her step-mother.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Ramita said she wished she didn't have to meet her step-mother.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence uses the structure "I wish + Simple Past", which expresses a present unreal wish/regret.

• Rule — Reported Speech with "Wish": When a sentence begins with "I wish", the reporting verb "wish" changes to "wished", but the tense of the clause AFTER "wish" does NOT change further back — it remains as it is, because "wish" clauses already express a hypothetical/unreal situation.
◦ Direct: I wish I didn't have to meet my step-mother.
◦ Indirect: She wished she didn't have to meet her step-mother.

• Pronoun changes: "I" → "she"; "my" → "her", since the reporter is speaking about Ramita.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "she hadn't have to meet" is grammatically wrong; "hadn't have to" is not a valid verb form in English.

• Option 2: "she wished she didn't meet" incorrectly drops "have to", changing the meaning from "obligation to meet" to simply "not meeting", which distorts the original sense.

• Option 4: "she wished hadn't met" wrongly shifts the tense to Past Perfect ("hadn't met") and also omits the subject "she" before "hadn't", making it ungrammatical.

NOTE

• Sentences with "wish" + Simple Past (present unreal wish) do NOT shift tense further in reported speech, unlike ordinary statements.

• Similarly, "If only" sentences and "It's time" sentences also retain their special tense forms when converted to indirect speech.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Music can improve mood, decrease pain and anxiety, and facilitate opportunities for emotional expression. Research (1)______ that music can benefit our physical and mental health in numerous ways. Music can (2)______ the brain’s production of the hormone dopamine. This increased dopamine production helps (3)________ feelings of anxiety and depression. Music is processed directly by the amygdala, which is the part of the brain (4)________ in mood and emotions. By reducing stress levels and providing a strong competing stimulus to the pain (5)________ that enter the brain, music therapy can assist in pain management.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. suggests.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "suggests" fits the context, meaning that research indicates or points towards a conclusion, without claiming absolute proof — an appropriately cautious tone for reporting research findings.

• Collocation: "Research suggests that..." is a standard, natural academic collocation used to introduce findings.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "interprets" means to explain the meaning of something; research does not "interpret that" a fact — it studies and reports findings, so this does not fit the structure.

• Option 3: "dreams" makes no logical sense with "research" as the subject; research cannot "dream" a fact.

• Option 4: "focuses" would require the preposition "on" ("focuses on"), not "that", making it grammatically incompatible with the given sentence structure.

NOTE

• Common collocations for reporting findings: "Research shows/suggests/indicates/reveals that..."

• Avoid absolute verbs like "proves" in academic writing unless the evidence is conclusive; "suggests" is preferred for indicating probability.

Music can improve mood, decrease pain and anxiety, and facilitate opportunities for emotional expression. Research (1)______ that music can benefit our physical and mental health in numerous ways. Music can (2)______ the brain’s production of the hormone dopamine. This increased dopamine production helps (3)________ feelings of anxiety and depression. Music is processed directly by the amygdala, which is the part of the brain (4)________ in mood and emotions. By reducing stress levels and providing a strong competing stimulus to the pain (5)________ that enter the brain, music therapy can assist in pain management.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. boost.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "boost" means to increase or improve something, which correctly fits the context of music increasing the brain's dopamine production.

• Collocation: "Boost production/levels" is a natural, commonly used phrase (e.g., "boost immunity", "boost energy levels").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "provide" means to supply or make something available; one cannot "provide production" — it does not collocate grammatically or logically with "production".

• Option 2: "furnish" means to supply or equip with something, typically used with concrete items (e.g., furnish a room), not abstract processes like "production".

• Option 3: "exhaust" means to use up completely or drain, which is the opposite of increasing dopamine production and contradicts the passage's positive tone about music's benefits.

NOTE

• Common collocations with "boost": boost morale, boost confidence, boost the economy, boost immunity.

• Context clue: the passage states music "can improve mood" and has positive effects, so the blank must carry a positive/increasing sense — ruling out "exhaust".

Music can (2)______ the brain’s production of the hormone dopamine. This increased dopamine production helps (3)________ feelings of anxiety and depression. Music is processed directly by the amygdala, which is the part of the brain (4)________ in mood and emotions. By reducing stress levels and providing a strong competing stimulus to the pain (5)________ that enter the brain, music therapy can assist in pain management.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. relieve.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "relieve" means to reduce or ease a feeling of distress, pain, or discomfort, which fits the passage's context — dopamine production helping to reduce anxiety and depression.

• Collocation: "Relieve feelings of anxiety/stress/pain" is a natural and common phrase in health-related writing.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "intensify" means to make something stronger or more intense, which is the opposite of what the passage describes (music reducing anxiety, not worsening it).

• Option 2: "amend" means to make minor changes to a text, law, or document — it does not logically apply to "feelings" at all.

• Option 3: "enhance" means to improve or intensify something; since anxiety and depression are negative feelings, "enhancing" them would contradict the passage's positive message about music's benefits.

NOTE

• Context clue: the opening line of the passage states music can "decrease pain and anxiety", so the blank must align with this reducing/easing sense.

• Common collocations with "relieve": relieve stress, relieve pain, relieve pressure, relieve symptoms.

Music can improve mood, decrease pain and anxiety, and facilitate opportunities for emotional expression. Research (1)______ that music can benefit our physical and mental health in numerous ways. Music can (2)______ the brain’s production of the hormone dopamine. This increased dopamine production helps (3)________ feelings of anxiety and depression. Music is processed directly by the amygdala, which is the part of the brain (4)________ in mood and emotions. By reducing stress levels and providing a strong competing stimulus to the pain (5)________ that enter the brain, music therapy can assist in pain management.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. involved.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "involved in" means taking part in or being connected with something, and is the standard collocation used to describe a body part's role in a process or function.

• Collocation: "The part of the brain involved in [function]" is a common, natural scientific phrase used to describe brain regions responsible for specific functions.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "concerned" typically collocates with "about" (worried about) or is used as "as far as X is concerned" — it does not fit the structure "concerned in mood and emotions".

• Option 3: "obsessed" means excessively preoccupied with something, typically used for people, not for a body part's biological function.

• Option 4: "accompanied" means going along with or escorting someone/something; it does not describe a functional biological role.

NOTE

• Common scientific collocations: "involved in a process", "responsible for a function", "associated with a condition."

• The amygdala is a well-known SSC/GK fact: it is the almond-shaped brain structure primarily associated with processing emotions, especially fear and pleasure.

Music is processed directly by the amygdala, which is the part of the brain (4)________ in mood and emotions. By reducing stress levels and providing a strong competing stimulus to the pain (5)________ that enter the brain, music therapy can assist in pain management.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. signals.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The noun "signals" correctly completes the phrase "pain signals", referring to the nerve impulses that travel to the brain to indicate pain.

• Collocation: "Pain signals that enter the brain" is the standard scientific/medical phrase describing how the nervous system communicates pain.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "deter" is a verb meaning to discourage someone from doing something; it cannot function as a noun after "pain" in this sentence.

• Option 3: "deform" is a verb meaning to distort the shape of something; it does not fit grammatically or logically as a noun describing what "enters the brain".

• Option 4: "substance" means a physical material or matter; while grammatically it could be a noun, "pain substance" is not a meaningful or scientifically accurate phrase, unlike "pain signals".

NOTE

• The blank requires a plural noun (matching the verb "enter", not "enters"), which further confirms "signals" as correct over the singular option "substance".

• Related term: "Nociceptors" are the sensory receptors that detect pain and send pain signals to the brain — a fact occasionally tested in SSC General Awareness.
